title: PossibleCooker Lemon Chicken Orzo with Artichoke Sauce
description: Orzo cooks with chicken thighs in a smooth artichoke broth that becomes a cohesive, lemon-scented sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Trim fat and dice across the grain into 1/2-inch pieces.

ingredients.name: plain cooked artichoke hearts
ingredients.note: Use tender unseasoned hearts; remove leaves with fibrous tips.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: Keep warm and use only as needed.

steps.title: Puree the artichokes
steps.text: Blend {artichoke} with enough {broth} to make a pourable puree, then push through a sieve to remove remaining fibers.

steps.title: Bring the sauce to a simmer
steps.text: Add the puree, remaining {broth} and {garlic} to the PossibleCooker. Select Sear/Sauté HIGH with the lid off and bring to a gentle simmer, about 5–7 minutes.

steps.title: Start the chicken
steps.text: Slip {chicken} into the sauce, let the simmer return and cook for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the orzo in the sauce
steps.text: Stir {orzo} straight into the chicken sauce. Switch to Sear/Sauté LOW and simmer uncovered for 9–14 minutes, stirring the bottom frequently with a silicone spoon. Verify the orzo is tender and the largest chicken piece reaches at least 165°F. Add {topup} a splash at a time if the pasta absorbs the liquid early.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Fold the slurry into the bubbling sauce and stir gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon and the orzo still moves freely.

steps.title: Finish the orzo
steps.text: Turn the cooker off and fold in {parmesan} and {zest}. Serve immediately with the sauce pooled around the pasta.

notes: Make ahead: Puree the artichokes and refrigerate the base a day ahead; cook the orzo in it right before dinner. Option A uses lemon zest. For gentler Option B, replace it with finely chopped parsley. For dairy-free orzo leave out the Parmesan. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The orzo continues absorbing sauce after freezing and reheating. Freeze the artichoke broth on its own instead. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the chicken to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and follow the fridge reheating directions. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 416 kcal, 36.7 g protein, 50.0 g total carbohydrate, 6.9 g fat, 4.3 g fiber, 237 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
